Generalizable All Variables.

The codomain of a Π whose codomain is a family value f: in the environment of f, #1 $ #0 is f at the argument. The types of the arguments of a function shape and of their recursive results are such Πs (d_shfam, d_ihfam): their codomains are computed by the families, so no term is built.
Definition fam_cod : exp := a_app (a_var 1) (a_var 0).

Kind-Directed Evaluation

No proof is ever evaluated: a term of a propositional type is kept as it is written, with the environment it stands in, as the proof value ⋆ᵈ⟨M, ρ⟩. The places where a proof may stand inside a relevant term read the kind of what stands there off values or declarations, never off types: the argument of an application (arg_kind), a field of a record value (its declaration's record_field_kind), a local definition and an entry of a module body (their types), and a substitution's entry (its target context's type, eval_sub).
Every variable an environment binds carries its type (entry_type), which the readback of a kept proof reads the variable at; the type is a closure, evaluated only there.
The number of values a constructor of the member Mk of D takes before its arguments: all the member's parameters, the uniform ones only at a record view.
Definition con_param_count (D : ind_decl) (Mk : imember) : nat :=
  match im_head Mk with mh_record _ _ _ => ind_nu D | _ => im_np D Mk end.

The kind of the n-th argument of the constructor c of the member Mk, as the declaration classifies it; a recursive argument is of a universe.
Definition con_arg_kind (Mk : imember) (c : string) (n : nat) : abs_kind :=
  match ind_con Mk c with
  | Some gs => match List.nth_error gs n with Some (ca_arg r _) => r | _ => ak_relevant end
  | None => ak_relevant
  end.

The global module at p, given args, lacks no parameter of its telescope. A term member is selected from a saturated global module only; one lacking a parameter gives a member closure, as a local closure lacking one does.
Definition module_saturated (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) (p : qname) (args : list domain) : Prop :=
  forall T Φ, gc_loc Θ Ξ p = Some (T, Φ) -> List.length T <= List.length args.

The kind of the n-th parameter of a telescope T, outermost first: ak_level at an assumption tagged ak_level, ak_relevant at every other entry and past the telescope. Parameters are never propositional by the typing rules (params_evaluated: relevant or levels), so at a typed declaration this is the kind the assumption is tagged with; at an entry tagged ak_propositional, which no well-typed term reaches, the value ak_relevant is junk, accepted so that a type former's arguments are always evaluated (tele_param_kind_evaluated).
Definition tele_param_kind (T : list centry) (n : nat) : abs_kind :=
  match List.nth_error T n with Some (ce_ass ak_level _) => ak_level | _ => ak_relevant end.

A parameter's kind is evaluated.
Lemma tele_param_kind_evaluated : forall T n, evaluated_kind (tele_param_kind T n).
Proof. intros; unfold tele_param_kind; destruct (List.nth_error T n) as [[[] | | | ] |]; constructor. Qed.

The kind of the next parameter of the module value h, one lacking parameters: for a local module closure, the last entry of its remaining telescope; for a global module, the entry of its telescope after its arguments; for a submodule's closure, its module's. As in tele_param_kind, a parameter of a type of levels is of ak_level and every other one of ak_relevant: module parameters are never propositional by the typing rules, so at an entry tagged ak_propositional, which no well-typed term reaches, the value ak_relevant is junk.
Fixpoint dmod_param_kind (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) (h : dmod) : abs_kind :=
  match h with
  | dm_local Δ _ _ => tele_param_kind (List.rev Δ) 0
  | dm_global p args =>
      match gc_loc Θ Ξ p with
      | Some (T, _) => tele_param_kind (List.rev T) (List.length args)
      | None => ak_relevant
      end
  | dm_member h _ => dmod_param_kind Θ Ξ h
  end.

The kind of the next argument a function value takes: the kind of a function's own domain or of a neutral's Π domain; for a type former of a group or of a record, and for a constructor before its arguments, the kind of the next parameter as the declaration tags it (tele_param_kind): a parameter of a type of levels is of ak_level; the stored kind of a constructor's next argument; and for the member of a module value lacking a parameter, that parameter's kind (dmod_param_kind). Every other function value takes arguments that are evaluated (ak_relevant).
Definition arg_kind (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) (f : domain) : abs_kind :=
  match f with
  | d_fn a _ _ => domain_kind a
  | d_neut (d_pi _ _ a _ _) _ => domain_kind a
  | d_ind p k vs =>
      match ind_lookup Θ Ξ p with
      | Some D =>
          match ind_member D k with
          | Some Mk => tele_param_kind (List.rev (im_params D Mk)) (List.length vs)
          | None => ak_relevant
          end
      | None => ak_relevant
      end
  | d_record p ns =>
      match record_lookup Θ Ξ p with
      | Some R => tele_param_kind (List.rev (record_params R)) (List.length ns)
      | None => ak_relevant
      end
  | d_con p k c vs =>
      match ind_lookup Θ Ξ p with
      | Some D =>
          match ind_member D k with
          | Some Mk =>
              if Nat.ltb (List.length vs) (con_param_count D Mk)
              then tele_param_kind (List.rev (im_params D Mk)) (List.length vs)
              else con_arg_kind Mk c (List.length vs - con_param_count D Mk)
          | None => ak_relevant
          end
      | None => ak_relevant
      end
  | d_member h _ => dmod_param_kind Θ Ξ h
  | _ => ak_relevant
  end.

A type former takes arguments of an evaluated kind: its parameters.
Lemma arg_kind_ind_evaluated : forall Θ Ξ p k vs, evaluated_kind (arg_kind Θ Ξ (d_ind p k vs)).
Proof.
  intros; cbn [arg_kind]; destruct (ind_lookup Θ Ξ p) as [D |]; [ destruct (ind_member D k) |];
    first [ apply tele_param_kind_evaluated | constructor ].
Qed.

Lemma arg_kind_record_evaluated : forall Θ Ξ p ns, evaluated_kind (arg_kind Θ Ξ (d_record p ns)).
Proof.
  intros; cbn [arg_kind]; destruct (record_lookup Θ Ξ p); first [ apply tele_param_kind_evaluated | constructor ].
Qed.

A module value lacking a parameter takes an argument of an evaluated kind.
Lemma dmod_param_kind_evaluated : forall Θ Ξ h, evaluated_kind (dmod_param_kind Θ Ξ h).
Proof.
  intros Θ Ξ h; induction h as [p args | Δ D ρ | h IH ch]; cbn [dmod_param_kind];
    [ destruct (gc_loc Θ Ξ p) as [[T Φ] |] | |]; first [ apply tele_param_kind_evaluated | constructor | exact IH ].
Qed.

The proof a member x of a saturated module is, kept as its selection from the module bound at #0: a proof member is never evaluated, so its value is this proof in an environment holding the module at #0.
Definition member_proof (x : string) : exp := a_mem (me_var 0) x.

The environment a proof member of a global module p at the arguments args is kept over (eval_sel_global_proof): the arguments, at p's parameter telescope T (innermost first, as gc_loc gives it), then the module at #0, stored at its alias applied to them, a unit written over the arguments. So every entry is written over its own tail, and readback binds the arguments, then the module.
Definition global_proof_env (p : qname) (T : list centry) (args : list domain) : env :=
  env_tele nil (List.rev T) args ↦ᵐ dm_global p args ⦂ gu_mk nil (md_alias (me_apps (qname_mod p) (vars_from 0 (List.length args)))).

The Types of the Variables an Eliminator Binds

A branch binds the non-uniform parameters of its member, the arguments of its constructor and their recursive results; a motive binds the member's non-uniform parameters and the scrutinee. Their types are closures over the declaration's telescopes, at the uniform parameters ups (decl_env); none is evaluated. At a declared member the types are those of the values. REVISIT at a view: the values are the container's and the telescopes the view's.
The environment of a group's uniform parameters ups.
Definition decl_env (D : ind_decl) (ups : list domain) : env := env_tele nil (List.rev (ind_uparams D)) ups.

The arguments vs of a constructor of kinds gs, with their types: a non-recursive one the type its declaration gives, in ρ extended by the non-recursive arguments before it; a recursive one the type of its shape there, at the uniform parameters ups of the group at p.
Fixpoint cargs_entries (p : qname) (ups : list domain) (ρ : env) (gs : list carg) (vs : list domain) : list (domain * entry_type) :=
  match vs with
  | nil => nil
  | v :: vs' =>
      match gs with
      | ca_arg _ A :: gs' => (v, entry_type_closure A ρ) :: cargs_entries p ups (ρ ↦ v ⦂ entry_type_closure A ρ) gs' vs'
      | ca_rec t :: gs' => (v, entry_type_shape p ups ρ t) :: cargs_entries p ups ρ gs' vs'
      | nil => (v, entry_type_none) :: cargs_entries p ups ρ nil vs'
      end
  end.

The types of the recursive results of the arguments vs of kinds gs: one per leaf path of each recursive argument, the motives As in ρm, the shape's components in ρ, which a non-recursive argument extends.
Fixpoint ihs_types (D : ind_decl) (p : qname) (ups : list domain) (ρm : env) (As : list exp)
    (ρ : env) (gs : list carg) (vs : list domain) : list entry_type :=
  match gs, vs with
  | ca_arg _ A :: gs', v :: vs' => ihs_types D p ups ρm As (ρ ↦ v ⦂ entry_type_closure A ρ) gs' vs'
  | ca_rec t :: gs', v :: vs' =>
      List.map (fun i => entry_type_induction_hypothesis ρm As p ups ρ t v i) (List.seq 0 (List.length (shape_leaves (rview_leaves D) 0 t)))
        ++ ihs_types D p ups ρm As ρ gs' vs'
  | _, _ => nil
  end.

pair_values_with_types vs ts: each value of vs paired with the type at its position in ts; a value past the end of ts is paired with no type (entry_type_none).
Fixpoint pair_values_with_types (vs : list domain) (ts : list entry_type) : list (domain * entry_type) :=
  match vs with
  | nil => nil
  | v :: vs' => (v, List.hd entry_type_none ts) :: pair_values_with_types vs' (List.tl ts)
  end.

The values of the typed lists of entries evaluation extends environments by: the values given, whatever their types.
Lemma cargs_entries_values : forall p ups ρ gs vs, List.map fst (cargs_entries p ups ρ gs vs) = vs.
Proof. intros p ups ρ gs vs; revert ρ gs; induction vs as [| v vs IH]; intros ρ [| [] gs]; cbn; f_equal; auto. Qed.

Lemma pair_values_with_types_values : forall vs ts, List.map fst (pair_values_with_types vs ts) = vs.
Proof. induction vs as [| v vs IH]; intros; cbn; [ reflexivity | rewrite IH; reflexivity ]. Qed.

A member of a suffix of a list is a member of the list.
Lemma in_skipn_in : forall {A : Type} n (l : list A) x, In x (List.skipn n l) -> In x l.
Proof. intros A n; induction n as [| n IH]; intros [| y l] x H; cbn in H; auto; right; exact (IH _ _ H). Qed.

A member of a prefix is a member of the list.
Lemma in_firstn_in : forall {A : Type} n (l : list A) x, In x (List.firstn n l) -> In x l.
Proof.
  intros A n; induction n as [| n IH]; intros [| y l] x H; cbn in H; try contradiction.
  destruct H as [<- | H]; [ left; reflexivity | right; exact (IH _ _ H) ].
Qed.

The variables of a branch of the member Mj of the group D at p, at the uniform parameters ups, the motives As in ρm: the non-uniform parameters ns, the arguments vs of kinds gs and the recursive results ihs, with their types.
Definition branch_entries (D : ind_decl) (Mj : imember) (p : qname) (ups : list domain) (As : list exp) (ρm : env)
    (gs : list carg) (ns vs ihs : list domain) : list (domain * entry_type) :=
  let nts := tele_entries (decl_env D ups) (List.rev (im_nparams Mj)) ns in
  let ρa := env_extend_typed (decl_env D ups) nts in
  nts ++ cargs_entries p ups ρa gs vs ++ pair_values_with_types ihs (ihs_types D p ups ρm As ρa gs vs).

The variables of a motive of the member Mk of D at the uniform parameters ups: the non-uniform parameters ns, and a scrutinee m of the type a.
Definition motive_entries (D : ind_decl) (Mk : imember) (ups ns : list domain) (a m : domain) : list (domain * entry_type) :=
  tele_entries (decl_env D ups) (List.rev (im_nparams Mk)) ns ++ (m, entry_type_value a) :: nil.

The Kinds of Members of Module Values

Selection tells a member's kind (a term of a sort, a module, or both) without a type: the kind of a member is read off the module value and the syntax of the units it closes over. A body is read through the entries it makes (kinds_env), as evaluation would but with no value for any definition, so that no term is evaluated: a kind does not depend on the values of terms, nor on a module's arguments, which are terms (kinds_pads). The bodies read are expanded, each local open replaced by the definitions it stores (gunit_expand), as evaluation closes them (eval_close_body). The relations read a closure or a submodule closure as selection on module values does (eval_selm).
The closure of a unit over ρ, as kinds read it (through its expansion, dmod_member_kind_local): a saturated alias is left as a closure, which kinds read through.
Definition dm_clo (U : gunit) (ρ : env) : dmod :=
  match U with gu_mk Δ D => dm_local Δ D ρ end.

n pads for parameters, terms whose values kinds never read, over ρ.
Definition kinds_pads (n : nat) (ρ : env) : env := List.repeat absent_entry n ++ ρ.

The entry a body's entry y adds over ρ, as kinds read it, as body_ctx binds it: a module, its closure; an inductive or a record type, the closure of the alias of its module; a definition with a module part, the closure of its unit with no term value; a definition, a pad (absent_entry).
Definition kinds_body_entry (ρ : env) (y : string) (E : gentry) : dentry :=
  match E with
  | ge_mod _ U => de_mod (dm_clo U ρ) U
  | ge_ind _ pq _ _ _ =>
      let U := gu_mk nil (md_alias (qname_mod (qname_sibling pq y))) in de_mod (dm_clo U ρ) U
  | ge_record _ p _ _ => let U := gu_mk nil (md_alias (qname_mod p)) in de_mod (dm_clo U ρ) U
  | ge_def_mod _ _ _ U => de_dm d_prop entry_type_none (dm_clo U ρ) U
  | _ => absent_entry
  end.

The kind of a member with a term part and a module part, by its module part's kind at the empty chain: a module makes it member_kind_dm. For a typed program the module part is always a module, so this is always member_kind_dm; the other cases exist only so that the kind theorems (kind_eval) hold without typing, of module parts that are no modules.
Definition dm_of (k : member_kind) : member_kind :=
  match k with
  | member_kind_mod => member_kind_dm
  | _ => k
  end.

Inductive dmod_member_kind (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : dmod -> list string -> member_kind -> Prop :=
A chain of a global module, read off the global context one name at a time, as selection on module values reads it (eval_selm): the path reached names a definition, a term, or a body module or an open frame, a module; a member with a term part and a module part (dm_path) is one, named from its parent, and a chain through it is read in its module part; a chain through an alias is read in the alias past it. At the empty chain a module value, whatever member it is the module part of, is a module. The path names a definition: a term of its sort
| dmod_member_kind_global_here_def : forall p args b pv ra A B,
    gc_resolve Θ Ξ p = Some (ge_def b pv ra A B) ->
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_global p args) nil (member_kind_term ra)
The path names a body module or an open frame: a module
| dmod_member_kind_global_here_mod : forall p args,
    (exists T oD, gc_module Θ Ξ p = Some (mr_body T oD)) \/ (exists TΦ, gc_frame Ξ p = Some TΦ) ->
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_global p args) nil member_kind_mod
The member y of the module at the path is a definition with a module part stored in place (its module part a body, located by gc_loc): a definition with a module part
| dmod_member_kind_global_here_dm : forall p args y TΦ,
    dm_path Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) ->
    gc_loc Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) = Some TΦ ->
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_global p args) (y :: nil) member_kind_dm
The member y is an alias, other than the module part of a definition at the end of the chain: the chain after y is read in the alias, expanded
| dmod_member_kind_global_alias_case : forall p args y ch U k,
    gc_module Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) = Some (mr_alias U) ->
    ch <> nil \/ ~ dm_path Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) ->
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ nil (gunit_expand U) ch k ->
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_global p args) (y :: ch) k
A definition with a module part stored as an alias: dm_of its alias's kind, expanded
| dmod_member_kind_global_alias_dm : forall p args y U k,
    gc_module Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) = Some (mr_alias U) ->
    dm_path Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) ->
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ nil (gunit_expand U) nil k ->
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_global p args) (y :: nil) (dm_of k)
The member y is located in place (a body, a frame or a definition), and the chain does not stop at the module part of a definition: the rest of the chain is read at the path of y
| dmod_member_kind_global_step : forall p args y ch k,
    (exists TΦ, gc_loc Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) = Some TΦ) \/
    (exists b pv ra A B, gc_resolve Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) = Some (ge_def b pv ra A B)) ->
    ch <> nil \/ ~ dm_path Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) ->
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_global (qname_app p (y :: nil)) args) ch k ->
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_global p args) (y :: ch) k
A closure, by its unit, expanded.
| dmod_member_kind_local : forall Δ D ρ ch k,
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (gunit_expand (gu_mk Δ D)) ch k ->
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_local Δ D ρ) ch k
A submodule closure, by the longer chain; at the empty chain it is a module, its member's module part when that member has a term part too. The longer chain, unless it is the empty chain at a definition with a module part
| dmod_member_kind_member : forall h ch0 ch k,
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ h (ch0 ++ ch) k ->
    ch <> nil \/ k <> member_kind_dm ->
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_member h ch0) ch k
The empty chain at a definition with a module part: the closure is its module part, a module
| dmod_member_kind_member_dm : forall h ch0,
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ h ch0 member_kind_dm ->
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_member h ch0) nil member_kind_mod
with gunit_member_kind (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : env -> gunit -> list string -> member_kind -> Prop :=
A body itself, at the empty chain: a module
| gunit_member_kind_self : forall ρ Δ sm Φ, gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (gu_mk Δ (md_body sm Φ)) nil member_kind_mod
A definition of the body: a term of its sort
| gunit_member_kind_def : forall ρ Δ sm Φ Φ' x b pv ra A B,
    gm_prefix_upto Φ x = Some (gm_ext Φ' x (ge_def b pv ra A B)) ->
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (gu_mk Δ (md_body sm Φ)) (x :: nil) (member_kind_term ra)
A submodule of the body: the rest of the chain read in its unit, in the environment of the entries before it
| gunit_member_kind_mod : forall ρ Δ sm Φ Φ' y pm Uy ρ1 ch k,
    gm_prefix_upto Φ y = Some (gm_ext Φ' y (ge_mod pm Uy)) ->
    kinds_env Θ Ξ (kinds_pads (List.length Δ) ρ) Φ' ρ1 ->
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ1 (gunit_expand Uy) ch k ->
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (gu_mk Δ (md_body sm Φ)) (y :: ch) k
A definition with a module part is one (dm_of its module part's kind), and a chain through it is read in its module part, as at the global level. A definition with a module part of the body, at the end of the chain: dm_of the kind of its module part
| gunit_member_kind_dm_here : forall ρ Δ sm Φ Φ' y pv A M Uy ρ1 k,
    gm_prefix_upto Φ y = Some (gm_ext Φ' y (ge_def_mod pv A M Uy)) ->
    kinds_env Θ Ξ (kinds_pads (List.length Δ) ρ) Φ' ρ1 ->
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ1 (gunit_expand Uy) nil k ->
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (gu_mk Δ (md_body sm Φ)) (y :: nil) (dm_of k)
A definition with a module part of the body, the chain going on: the rest of the chain read in its module part, in the environment of the entries before it
| gunit_member_kind_dm_step : forall ρ Δ sm Φ Φ' y pv A M Uy ρ1 ch k,
    gm_prefix_upto Φ y = Some (gm_ext Φ' y (ge_def_mod pv A M Uy)) ->
    ch <> nil ->
    kinds_env Θ Ξ (kinds_pads (List.length Δ) ρ) Φ' ρ1 ->
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ1 (gunit_expand Uy) ch k ->
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (gu_mk Δ (md_body sm Φ)) (y :: ch) k
An alias unit: the chain is read in its target
| gunit_member_kind_alias : forall ρ Δ E ch k,
    modexp_member_kind Θ Ξ (kinds_pads (List.length Δ) ρ) E ch k ->
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (gu_mk Δ (md_alias E)) ch k
with modexp_member_kind (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : env -> modexp -> list string -> member_kind -> Prop :=
A unit: the chain read in the global module of the unit
| modexp_member_kind_unit : forall ρ fp ch k,
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (dm_global (q_abs fp nil) nil) ch k ->
    modexp_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (me_unit fp) ch k
A module slot: the chain read in the module value of the slot
| modexp_member_kind_var : forall ρ x ch k,
    dmod_member_kind Θ Ξ (env_mod ρ x) ch k ->
    modexp_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (me_var x) ch k
A literal unit: the chain read in the unit, expanded
| modexp_member_kind_lit : forall ρ U ch k,
    gunit_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (gunit_expand U) ch k ->
    modexp_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (me_lit U) ch k
A selection, by the longer chain; at the empty chain it is a module, its member's module part when that member has a term part too. The longer chain, unless it is the empty chain at a definition with a module part
| modexp_member_kind_mem : forall ρ H y ch k,
    modexp_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ H (y :: ch) k ->
    ch <> nil \/ k <> member_kind_dm ->
    modexp_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (me_mem H y) ch k
The empty chain at a definition with a module part: the selection is its module part, a module
| modexp_member_kind_mem_dm : forall ρ H y,
    modexp_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ H (y :: nil) member_kind_dm ->
    modexp_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (me_mem H y) nil member_kind_mod
An application: the chain read in the module applied
| modexp_member_kind_app : forall ρ H N ch k,
    modexp_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ H ch k ->
    modexp_member_kind Θ Ξ ρ (me_app H N) ch k
The environment an expanded body makes, as kinds read it: an entry each body entry adds (kinds_body_entry).
with kinds_env (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : env -> gmod -> env -> Prop :=
The empty body adds nothing
| kinds_env_nil : forall ρ, kinds_env Θ Ξ ρ gm_nil ρ
An entry adds its kinds_body_entry
| kinds_env_ext : forall ρ Φ ρ1 y E,
    kinds_env Θ Ξ ρ Φ ρ1 ->
    kinds_env Θ Ξ ρ (gm_ext Φ y E) (kinds_body_entry ρ1 y E :: ρ1).

Scheme dmod_member_kind_mut_ind := Induction for dmod_member_kind Sort Prop
with gunit_member_kind_mut_ind := Induction for gunit_member_kind Sort Prop
with modexp_member_kind_mut_ind := Induction for modexp_member_kind Sort Prop
with kinds_env_mut_ind := Induction for kinds_env Sort Prop.
Combined Scheme kind_mut_ind from dmod_member_kind_mut_ind, gunit_member_kind_mut_ind, modexp_member_kind_mut_ind, kinds_env_mut_ind.

#[export]
Hint Constructors dmod_member_kind gunit_member_kind modexp_member_kind kinds_env : mctt.

Evaluation of Expressions

The relations are mutually defined: evaluation of terms, the eliminator's cases and semantic application; evaluation of module expressions and the operations on module values (application, selection of a submodule or a member, along a chain); and the environment a body unit's members see. All are relative to the global context Θ ⍮ Ξ, which does not change during NbE. A global is resolved by lookup in Θ ⍮ Ξ: a transparent definition unfolds to its body, and any other global is a neutral at its type. No rule applies a syntactic operation such as substitution to a term, and none builds syntax: a global is looked up, never rebuilt.
A module value is saturated when it has as many arguments as its unit has parameters. Selection on a saturated module is δ: it gives the bound value, by evaluating the body up to the member, or by selecting from the alias's target. Selection on an unsaturated one gives a member closure (d_member, dm_member), which the remaining arguments complete. A global module needs neither: its members are stored generalized over its parameters, so selection applies the generalized member to the arguments there are.
Inductive eval_exp (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : exp -> env -> domain -> Prop :=
A universe is its own value.
| eval_exp_typ :
  `( ⟦ Typeω@i ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ 𝕌ω@i )
A small universe evaluates its level.
| eval_exp_univ :
  `( ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ l ->
     ⟦ Type⟨M⟩ ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ 𝕌@l )
Level is a value.
| eval_exp_level :
  `( ⟦ Level@n ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ Levelᵈ@n )
So is the sort of the types of levels.
| eval_exp_level_sort :
  `( ⟦ LevelSort ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ LevelSortᵈ )
A level literal is the flat level with that constant and no atom.
| eval_exp_llit :
  `( ⟦ 𝕃ᵒ o ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ domain_level_lit o )
The level operations only flatten: they add to the offsets, or join the constants and concatenate the atoms. Canonicalisation is readback's.
| eval_exp_succl :
  `( ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     ⟦ succl M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ domain_level_suc m )
The join of two levels: the flat join of their values.
| eval_exp_maxl :
  `( ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     ⟦ N ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ n ->
     ⟦ maxl M N ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ domain_level_max m n )
A variable is read off the environment.
| eval_exp_var :
  `( ⟦ #x ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ x )
Prop is a value.
| eval_exp_prop :
  `( ⟦ Propₘ ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ Propᵈ )
⊤ is a value.
| eval_exp_True :
  `( ⟦ ⊤ ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ⊤ᵈ )
The introduction of ⊤ is a proof, kept as it is.
| eval_exp_tt :
  `( ⟦ a_tt ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ⋆ᵈ⟨a_tt, ρ⟩ )
⊥ is a value.
| eval_exp_False :
  `( ⟦ ⊥ ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ⊥ᵈ )
Ex falso never evaluates its proof: it is stuck at its type, on the proof kept as it is.
| eval_exp_absurd :
  `( ⟦ C ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ c ->
     ⟦ efq M return C ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ⇑ c (efqᵈ ⋆ᵈ⟨M, ρ⟩ return c) )
A Σₚ evaluates its first component and closes over its second.
| eval_exp_and :
  `( ⟦ P ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ p ->
     ⟦ Σₚ P Q ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ Σₚᵈ p ρ Q )
The proof of a conjunction is kept as it is; its parts are not evaluated.
| eval_exp_conj :
  `( ⟦ a_conj P Q M N ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ⋆ᵈ⟨a_conj P Q M N, ρ⟩ )
So is the proof of its first component.
| eval_exp_left :
  `( ⟦ a_left M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ⋆ᵈ⟨a_left M, ρ⟩ )
And that of its second.
| eval_exp_right :
  `( ⟦ a_right M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ⋆ᵈ⟨a_right M, ρ⟩ )
A tagged proof is its proof: the tag has no effect.
| eval_exp_proof_tag :
  `( ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     ⟦ a_proof P M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m )
The type former and a constructor of a member of a group of inductive types are values, with no argument yet.
| eval_exp_indty :
  `( ⟦ a_ind p k ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_ind p k nil )
A constructor, with no argument yet, when it is a value of its own before any argument (im_starts).
| eval_exp_con :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D k = Some Mk ->
     im_starts D Mk = true ->
     ⟦ a_con p k c ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_con p k c nil )
A constructor of a view of a group with no uniform parameters is at once the container's, at the view's arguments.
| eval_exp_con_view :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_view qc k Is vm ->
     ind_nu D = 0 ->
     ⟦ Is ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ nil ↘ cups ->
     ⟦ a_con p j c ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_con qc k c cups )
The constructor of a record view of a group with no uniform parameters, of a record with fields: a value of its own, waiting for the fields.
| eval_exp_con_rview :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_record qr Is fl ->
     ind_nu D = 0 ->
     0 < List.length fl ->
     ⟦ a_con p j c ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_con p j c nil )
The constructor of a record view of a group with no uniform parameters, of a record without fields: at once the empty tuple.
| eval_exp_con_rview_empty :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_record qr Is nil ->
     ind_nu D = 0 ->
     ⟦ a_con p j c ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_tuple nil )
The eliminator evaluates its scrutinee, then eliminates the value, by the blocks of its group, at the group's uniform parameters it carries.
| eval_exp_elim :
  `( ⟦ Us ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ups ->
     ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     ⟦elim m at j of p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r ->
     ⟦ a_elim ak_relevant p Us j Bks M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
An eliminator into propositions is a proof, kept as it is.
| eval_exp_elim_proof :
  `( ⟦ a_elim ak_propositional p Us j Bks M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ⋆ᵈ⟨a_elim ak_propositional p Us j Bks M, ρ⟩ )
A Π evaluates its domain and closes over its codomain, at its kinds.
| eval_exp_pi :
  `( ⟦ A ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ a ->
     ⟦ a_pi κd κc A B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_pi κd κc a ρ B )
A function evaluates its domain and closes over its body: it keeps its domain, so that its application can tell a proof argument.
| eval_exp_fn :
  `( ⟦ A ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ a ->
     ⟦ λ A M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ λᵈ a ρ M )
An application of a function taking an evaluated argument applies the value of the function to that of the argument.
| eval_exp_app :
  `( ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     evaluated_kind (arg_kind Θ Ξ m) ->
     ⟦ N ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ n ->
     $| m & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     ⟦ M $ N ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
An application of a function taking a proof applies it to the proof kept as it is; the argument is not evaluated.
| eval_exp_app_proof :
  `( ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     arg_kind Θ Ξ m = ak_propositional ->
     $| m & ⋆ᵈ⟨N, ρ⟩ | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     ⟦ M $ N ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
A local definition at a type of an evaluated kind extends the environment by the value of its body, at its type; nothing is substituted.
| eval_exp_let :
  `( ⟦ A ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ a ->
     evaluated_kind (domain_kind a) ->
     ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     ⟦ B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↦ m ⦂ entry_type_value a ↘ r ->
     ⟦ ℓ A ≔ M in B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
One at a proposition binds its body, a proof, kept as it is.
| eval_exp_let_proof :
  `( ⟦ A ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ a ->
     domain_kind a = ak_propositional ->
     ⟦ B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↦ ⋆ᵈ⟨M, ρ⟩ ⦂ entry_type_value a ↘ r ->
     ⟦ ℓ A ≔ M in B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
A local module extends it by the unit's closure, at the unit.
| eval_exp_let_mod :
  `( ⟦ Δ ⊢ D ⟧ᶜ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ h ->
     ⟦ B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↦ᵐ h ⦂ gu_mk Δ D ↘ r ->
     ⟦ ℓₘ (gu_mk Δ D) in B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
A local definition with a module part extends it by the value of its body, at its type, and the value of the unit's literal, at the unit, as an entry of the context's initial environment is (initial_env).
| eval_exp_let_dm :
  `( ⟦ A ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ a ->
     ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     ⟦ me_lit U ⟧ᵐ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ h ->
     ⟦ B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↦ᵈ m ⦂ entry_type_value a ‖ h ⦂ U ↘ r ->
     ⟦ ℓᵈ A ≔ M ‖ U in B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
A member is read off the root of its module expression, then applied to the module's arguments: arguments commute with selection. Without arguments this is selection from the module's value. The parameters of a module are relevant, so its arguments are all evaluated, as eval_me_app evaluates them.
| eval_exp_mem :
  `( modexp_spine H = (R, args, pre) ->
     ⟦ R ⟧ᵐ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ h ->
     h ·ₜ* (pre ++ x :: nil) Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ f ->
     ⟦ args ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ns ->
     $*| f & ns | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     ⟦ a_mem H x ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
A record's type former is a value, with no argument yet.
| eval_exp_record :
  `( ⟦ a_record p ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_record p nil )
A record element is the tuple of its fields' values, by name, a propositional field kept as it is (eval_field_vals); the type it is annotated with is evaluated only to find the record, whose declaration stores the fields' sorts, and the value carries no parameters.
| eval_exp_tuple :
  `( ⟦ T ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_record p ns ->
     record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     eval_field_vals Θ Ξ (record_field_kinds R) (List.map snd fs) ρ vs ->
     ⟦ a_tuple T fs ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_tuple (List.combine (List.map fst fs) vs) )
A field: the field of the value.
| eval_exp_proj :
  `( ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     eval_proj Θ Ξ f m r ->
     ⟦ a_proj f M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
where "'⟦' e '⟧' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' r" := (eval_exp Θ Ξ e ρ r)
The field f of a value: of a tuple, the value of its first field so named; of a neutral of a record type, the neutral projection, at the field's type at the type's parameters and the neutral projections of the fields before it (read off the neutral's annotation, as a stuck eliminator's motive is).
with eval_proj (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : string -> domain -> domain -> Prop :=
A tuple: its field
| eval_proj_tuple :
  `( field_lookup vs f = Some r ->
     eval_proj Θ Ξ f (d_tuple vs) r )
A neutral: its projection, at the field's type
| eval_proj_neut :
  `( record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     field_index (record_fields R) f = Some k ->
     eval_neutral_fields Θ Ξ m (env_tele nil (List.rev (record_params R)) ns) (List.firstn (S k) (record_fields R)) rs ->
     List.nth_error rs k = Some r ->
     eval_proj Θ Ξ f (⇑ (d_record p ns) m) r )
eval_neutral_fields m ρ fl rs: the neutral projections rs of m at the fields fl, each at its type in ρ, the environment of the type's parameters and the projections of the fields before it.
with eval_neutral_fields (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : domain_ne -> env -> list (string * exp) -> list domain -> Prop :=
No field left
| eval_neutral_fields_nil :
  `( eval_neutral_fields Θ Ξ m ρ nil nil )
The next field's projection, at its type, then the rest after it
| eval_neutral_fields_cons :
  `( ⟦ T ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ a ->
     eval_neutral_fields Θ Ξ m (ρ ↦ ⇑ a (d_proj g m) ⦂ entry_type_closure T ρ) fl rs ->
     eval_neutral_fields Θ Ξ m ρ ((g, T) :: fl) (⇑ a (d_proj g m) :: rs) )
The eliminator of the group at p at its member j, on a value. The member is the declared member k of the group at q (im_ref): the group itself at a declared member, the container's at a view. On a constructor of it at all its parameters and arguments, the branch of the constructor in the member's block, with its non-uniform parameters, its arguments and the recursive results, each by the eliminator at the member of the group its argument is recursive in, as the group classifies the member's arguments. On a neutral of the member, a neutral at the motive's instance; the neutral records the parameters of its type, which readback needs, and the group's uniform parameters ups the eliminator carries.
with eval_elim (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : env -> qname -> list domain -> list eblock -> nat -> domain -> domain -> Prop :=
On a saturated constructor: its branch, at the non-uniform parameters, the arguments and the recursive results. The group's table of leaf paths is coherent (leaves_coherent D), a gate on the group, the twin of readback's rview_leaf_arity: the recursive results along the record views' fields are then as many as the branch binds (cargs_nrec).
| eval_elim_con :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_ref p j Mj = (pc, k) ->
     ind_lookup Θ Ξ pc = Some Dq ->
     ind_member Dq k = Some Mk ->
     ind_con Mj c = Some gs ->
     List.length vs = (im_np Dq Mk + List.length gs)%nat ->
     List.nth_error Bks j = Some b ->
     brs_lookup (eb_brs b) c = Some (n, B) ->
     n = (im_nn Mk + List.length gs + cargs_nrec D gs)%nat ->
     leaves_coherent D ->
     ⟦ihs skipn (im_np Dq Mk) vs of gs under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ihs ->
     ⟦ B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ env_extend_typed ρ (branch_entries D Mj p ups (blocks_motives Bks) ρ gs
                                    (skipn (ind_nu Dq) (firstn (im_np Dq Mk) vs)) (skipn (im_np Dq Mk) vs) ihs) ↘ r ->
     ⟦elim d_con pc k c vs at j of p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
On a neutral: a stuck eliminator, at the motive's instance. The motive's variables are typed by the eliminator's own telescope: its non-uniform parameters, the neutral's, at the member j of D at the eliminator's uniform parameters ups, and the scrutinee, the neutral itself, at the member's type at ups (eval_mref) and at those parameters; as the eliminator's typing rule checks the motive, as eval_ihty_self types it, and as readback reads it. So its entries read back at that admissible base whatever the neutral's annotation is, which the model does not constrain: for W (A : Type) : A → Type eliminated at ups = [ℕ], a neutral annotated W Bool x binds x at ℕ and itself at W ℕ x, where they read back, not at Bool and W Bool x. In a well-typed program the annotation and this instance agree, so only the model sees the difference. The values are the neutral's non-uniform parameters (List.skipn (ind_nu Dq) as') and the types are read at ups (motive_entries), as read_blocks_cons binds a block's motive.
| eval_elim_neut :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_ref p j Mj = (pc, k) ->
     ind_lookup Θ Ξ pc = Some Dq ->
     ind_member Dq k = Some Mk ->
     List.length as' = im_np Dq Mk ->
     List.nth_error Bks j = Some b ->
     eb_binder_count b = S (im_nn Mk) ->
     ⟦mref j of p ups ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ (pc, k, cups) ->
     ⟦ eb_motive b ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ env_extend_typed ρ (motive_entries D Mj ups (List.skipn (ind_nu Dq) as')
                                          (d_ind pc k (cups ++ List.skipn (ind_nu Dq) as')) (⇑ (d_ind pc k as') m)) ↘ a ->
     ⟦elim ⇑ (d_ind pc k as') m at j of p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ⇑ a (d_elim ρ Bks p ups j as' m) )
where "'⟦elim' m 'at' j 'of' p ups Bks '⟧' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' r" := (eval_elim Θ Ξ ρ p ups Bks j m r)
The recursive results of the arguments vs, one per leaf path of each recursive argument, in order.
with eval_ihs (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : env -> qname -> list domain -> list eblock -> list carg -> list domain -> list domain -> Prop :=
No argument, no result
| eval_ihs_nil :
  `( ⟦ihs nil of nil under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ nil )
A non-recursive argument has none
| eval_ihs_arg :
  `( ⟦ihs vs of gs under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ihs ->
     ⟦ihs v :: vs of ca_arg r T :: gs under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ihs )
A recursive argument has its recursive results
| eval_ihs_rec :
  `( ⟦ih v of t under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ihs1 ->
     ⟦ihs vs of gs under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ihs ->
     ⟦ihs v :: vs of ca_rec t :: gs under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ihs1 ++ ihs )
where "'⟦ihs' vs 'of' gs 'under' p ups Bks '⟧' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' r" := (eval_ihs Θ Ξ ρ p ups Bks gs vs r)
The recursive results of an argument v of shape t, one per leaf path: the eliminator at v, at the member the shape ends in; at a record view, those of the view's fields, at v's projections; at a function shape, the family of each recursive result at v's values.
with eval_ih (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : env -> qname -> list domain -> list eblock -> ptyp -> domain -> list domain -> Prop :=
At the end of a shape, at a member with a block: the eliminator at the member j
| eval_ih_self :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_is_rview Mj = false ->
     ⟦elim v at j of p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r ->
     ⟦ih v of pt_self j Ps under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r :: nil )
At the end of a shape, at a record view: the recursive results of its fields at the projections of v
| eval_ih_rview :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_record qr Is fl ->
     im_cons Mj = (c, gs) :: nil ->
     ⟦projs fl of v ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ ws ->
     ⟦ihs ws of gs under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ rs ->
     ⟦ih v of pt_self j Ps under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ rs )
At a function shape: the family of each recursive result of the rest at v's values, one per leaf path of the rest
| eval_ih_pi :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ⟦ih v of pt_pi B t under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ
       ↘ List.map (fun i => d_ihfn ρ Bks p ups t i v) (List.seq 0 (List.length (shape_leaves (rview_leaves D) 0 t))) )
where "'⟦ih' v 'of' t 'under' p ups Bks '⟧' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' r" := (eval_ih Θ Ξ ρ p ups Bks t v r)
The projections of a value at the fields fl, in order.
with eval_projs (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : list string -> domain -> list domain -> Prop :=
No field
| eval_projs_nil :
  `( ⟦projs nil of v ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ nil )
The first field's projection, then the rest
| eval_projs_cons :
  `( eval_proj Θ Ξ f v w ->
     ⟦projs fl of v ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ ws ->
     ⟦projs f :: fl of v ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ w :: ws )
where "'⟦projs' fl 'of' v '⟧' Θ '⍮' Ξ '↘' ws" := (eval_projs Θ Ξ fl v ws)
The member j of the group at p at the uniform parameters ups: the declared member k of the group at q at the uniform parameters pre (im_ref, im_pre), the group itself and ups at a declared member, the container's and the view's arguments at ups at a view.
with eval_mref (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : qname -> list domain -> nat -> (qname * nat * list domain) -> Prop :=
A declared member: itself, at ups
| eval_mref_decl :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_decl pm ->
     ⟦mref j of p ups ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ (p, j, ups) )
A view: the container's member, at the view's arguments at ups
| eval_mref_view :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_view qc k Is vm ->
     ⟦ Is ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ decl_env D ups ↘ cups ->
     ⟦mref j of p ups ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ (qc, k, cups) )
where "'⟦mref' j 'of' p ups '⟧' Θ '⍮' Ξ '↘' r" := (eval_mref Θ Ξ p ups j r)
The type of an argument of shape t in ρ, at the uniform parameters ups of the group at p: at the end, the member the shape ends in at the shape's non-uniform parameters: the container's type at a view, as every value and every neutral of a view is of the container's member. Readback reads an argument of a shape at the group's own member instead (read_shape).
with eval_shape_type (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : qname -> list domain -> env -> ptyp -> domain -> Prop :=
At the end: the member's type former at the shape's parameters
| eval_shape_type_self :
  `( ⟦ Ps ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ bs ->
     ⟦mref j of p ups ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ (pc, k, pre) ->
     ⟦shty pt_self j Ps of p ups ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_ind pc k (pre ++ bs) )
At the end, at a record view: the record type at the view's instance at ups
| eval_shape_type_rview :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_record qr Is fl ->
     ⟦ Is ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ decl_env D ups ↘ cups ->
     ⟦shty pt_self j Ps of p ups ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ d_record qr cups )
At a domain: a Π over it, of the shape family. The environment of the codomain fam_cod binds the family alone; it never holds a proof, so its entry is at no type (entry_type_none).
| eval_shape_type_pi :
  `( ⟦ B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ b ->
     ⟦shty pt_pi B t of p ups ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ Πᵈ{ak_relevant} b (nil ↦ d_shfam p ups ρ B t ⦂ entry_type_none) fam_cod )
where "'⟦shty' t 'of' p ups '⟧' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' r" := (eval_shape_type Θ Ξ p ups ρ t r)
The types of the recursive results of an argument v of shape t, one per leaf path, its components in ρ, of the group at p at the uniform parameters ups: the motive of the member the shape ends in, among As in ρm, at the shape's non-uniform parameters and v; at a record view, those of its fields at v's projections, their components over ups; at a function shape, a Π over the domain of each.
with eval_ihty (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : qname -> list domain -> env -> list exp -> env -> ptyp -> domain -> list domain -> Prop :=
At the end, at a member with a block: the member's motive at the shape's parameters and v
| eval_ihty_self :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_is_rview Mj = false ->
     ⟦ Ps ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ bs ->
     ⟦ List.nth j As a_prop ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮
       env_extend_typed ρm (tele_entries (decl_env D ups) (List.rev (im_nparams Mj)) bs ++ (v, entry_type_shape p ups ρ (pt_self j Ps)) :: nil) ↘ a ->
     ⟦ihty v of pt_self j Ps at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ a :: nil )
At the end, at a record view: those of its fields at v's projections
| eval_ihty_rview :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_record qr Is fl ->
     im_cons Mj = (c, gs) :: nil ->
     ⟦projs fl of v ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ ws ->
     ⟦ihtys ws of gs at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ decl_env D ups ↘ rs ->
     ⟦ihty v of pt_self j Ps at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ rs )
At a domain: a Π over it, of each recursive result's family
| eval_ihty_pi :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ⟦ B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ b ->
     ⟦ihty v of pt_pi B t at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ
       ↘ List.map (fun i => Πᵈ{ak_relevant} b (nil ↦ d_ihfam ρm As p ups ρ B t i v ⦂ entry_type_none) fam_cod)
           (List.seq 0 (List.length (shape_leaves (rview_leaves D) 0 t))) )
where "'⟦ihty' v 'of' t 'at' p ups 'under' ρm As '⟧' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' r" := (eval_ihty Θ Ξ p ups ρm As ρ t v r)
The types of the recursive results of the fields vs of a record view, of kinds gs, their components in ρ, which a non-recursive field extends.
with eval_ihtys (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : qname -> list domain -> env -> list exp -> env -> list carg -> list domain -> list domain -> Prop :=
No field, no result
| eval_ihtys_nil :
  `( ⟦ihtys nil of nil at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ nil )
A non-recursive field has none, and extends the components' environment
| eval_ihtys_arg :
  `( ⟦ihtys vs of gs at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↦ v ⦂ entry_type_closure T ρ ↘ rs ->
     ⟦ihtys v :: vs of ca_arg r T :: gs at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ rs )
A recursive field has those of its shape
| eval_ihtys_rec :
  `( ⟦ihty v of t at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ rs1 ->
     ⟦ihtys vs of gs at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ rs ->
     ⟦ihtys v :: vs of ca_rec t :: gs at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ rs1 ++ rs )
where "'⟦ihtys' vs 'of' gs 'at' p ups 'under' ρm As '⟧' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' r" := (eval_ihtys Θ Ξ p ups ρm As ρ gs vs r)
with eval_app (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : domain -> domain -> domain -> Prop :=
A function's body, at the argument.
| eval_app_fn :
  `( ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↦ n ⦂ entry_type_value a ↘ m ->
     $| λᵈ a ρ M & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ m )
A neutral applied, at the codomain's instance, a Π into an evaluated kind. No rule applies a proof: an application whose function is a proof is at a ∀, hence itself a proof, which kind-directed evaluation never evaluates.
| eval_app_neut :
  `( evaluated_kind κc ->
     ⟦ B ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↦ n ⦂ entry_type_value a ↘ b ->
     $| ⇑ (d_pi κd κc a ρ B) m & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ ⇑ b (m $ᵈ ⇓ a n) )
The type former takes a parameter it still lacks.
| eval_app_indty :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D k = Some Mk ->
     List.length as' < im_np D Mk ->
     $| d_ind p k as' & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ d_ind p k (as' ++ n :: nil) )
So does a record's type former.
| eval_app_record :
  `( record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     List.length ns < List.length (record_params R) ->
     $| d_record p ns & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ d_record p (ns ++ n :: nil) )
So does a constructor, a parameter or an argument.
| eval_app_con :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D k = Some Mk ->
     im_head Mk = mh_decl pm ->
     ind_con Mk c = Some gs ->
     List.length vs < (im_np D Mk + List.length gs)%nat ->
     $| d_con p k c vs & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ d_con p k c (vs ++ n :: nil) )
A constructor of a view takes the group's uniform parameters; at the last of them it is the container's, at the view's arguments there.
| eval_app_con_view :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_view qc k Is vm ->
     S (List.length vs) < ind_nu D ->
     $| d_con p j c vs & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ d_con p j c (vs ++ n :: nil) )
At the last uniform parameter, the container's constructor at the view's arguments
| eval_app_con_view_ups :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_view qc k Is vm ->
     S (List.length vs) = ind_nu D ->
     ⟦ Is ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ decl_env D (vs ++ n :: nil) ↘ cups ->
     $| d_con p j c vs & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ d_con qc k c cups )
The constructor of a record view takes the group's uniform parameters and the fields; before the last of them it waits for more
| eval_app_con_rview :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_record qr Is fl ->
     S (List.length vs) < ind_nu D + List.length fl ->
     $| d_con p j c vs & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ d_con p j c (vs ++ n :: nil) )
At the last one, the tuple of the fields, by name: a record value carries no parameters
| eval_app_con_rview_full :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_record qr Is fl ->
     S (List.length vs) = ind_nu D + List.length fl ->
     $| d_con p j c vs & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ d_tuple (List.combine fl (List.skipn (ind_nu D) (vs ++ n :: nil))) )
The i-th recursive result of a function shape, at the argument's value: the i-th of the rest's at the function's value there.
| eval_app_ihfn :
  `( $| f & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ fn ->
     ⟦ih fn of t under p ups Bks ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ rs ->
     List.nth_error rs i = Some r ->
     $| d_ihfn ρ Bks p ups t i f & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
The families of the types of an argument of a function shape and of its recursive result.
| eval_app_shfam :
  `( ⟦shty t of p ups ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↦ n ⦂ entry_type_closure B ρ ↘ a ->
     $| d_shfam p ups ρ B t & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ a )
The i-th recursive result's family, at the argument's value
| eval_app_ihfam :
  `( $| f & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ fn ->
     ⟦ihty fn of t at p ups under ρm As ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↦ n ⦂ entry_type_closure B ρ ↘ as' ->
     List.nth_error as' i = Some a ->
     $| d_ihfam ρm As p ups ρ B t i f & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ a )
A member closure takes the next argument of its module, and selects again.
| eval_app_member :
  `( $ᵐ| h & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ h' ->
     h' ·ₜ* ch Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     $| d_member h ch & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
where "'$|' m '&' n '|' Θ '⍮' Ξ '↘' r" := (eval_app Θ Ξ m n r)
with eval_exps (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : list exp -> env -> list domain -> Prop :=
No terms.
| eval_exps_nil :
  `( ⟦ nil ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ nil )
A term, then the rest.
| eval_exps_cons :
  `( ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     ⟦ Ms ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ms ->
     ⟦ M :: Ms ⟧* Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m :: ms )
where "'⟦' Ms '⟧*' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' ms" := (eval_exps Θ Ξ Ms ρ ms)
eval_app_args f Ms ρ r: f applied to the terms Ms in ρ, outermost first, is r; an argument the function at that point takes as a proof (arg_kind) is kept as it is, unevaluated, as in eval_exp_app_proof.
with eval_app_args (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : domain -> list exp -> env -> domain -> Prop :=
No argument: the function itself.
| eval_app_args_nil :
  `( eval_app_args Θ Ξ f nil ρ f )
An evaluated argument: its value applied, then the rest.
| eval_app_args_evaluated :
  `( evaluated_kind (arg_kind Θ Ξ f) ->
     ⟦ N ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ n ->
     $| f & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ g ->
     eval_app_args Θ Ξ g Ns ρ r ->
     eval_app_args Θ Ξ f (N :: Ns) ρ r )
A proof argument: the proof applied, kept as it is, then the rest.
| eval_app_args_proof :
  `( arg_kind Θ Ξ f = ak_propositional ->
     $| f & ⋆ᵈ⟨N, ρ⟩ | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ g ->
     eval_app_args Θ Ξ g Ns ρ r ->
     eval_app_args Θ Ξ f (N :: Ns) ρ r )
eval_field_vals rs Ms ρ vs: the values vs of the fields Ms of a record value, the field at the kind ak_propositional in rs a proof kept as it is, not evaluated (a kind past rs is ak_relevant).
with eval_field_vals (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : list abs_kind -> list exp -> env -> list domain -> Prop :=
No field.
| eval_field_vals_nil :
  `( eval_field_vals Θ Ξ rs nil ρ nil )
An evaluated field: its value, then the rest.
| eval_field_vals_evaluated :
  `( evaluated_kind (List.hd ak_relevant rs) ->
     ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ m ->
     eval_field_vals Θ Ξ (List.tl rs) Ms ρ ms ->
     eval_field_vals Θ Ξ rs (M :: Ms) ρ (m :: ms) )
A propositional field: the proof kept as it is, then the rest.
| eval_field_vals_proof :
  `( List.hd ak_relevant rs = ak_propositional ->
     eval_field_vals Θ Ξ (List.tl rs) Ms ρ ms ->
     eval_field_vals Θ Ξ rs (M :: Ms) ρ (⋆ᵈ⟨M, ρ⟩ :: ms) )
with eval_apps (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : domain -> list domain -> domain -> Prop :=
No arguments.
| eval_apps_nil :
  `( $*| m & nil | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ m )
The first argument, then the rest.
| eval_apps_cons :
  `( $| m & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ m1 ->
     $*| m1 & args | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     $*| m & n :: args | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
where "'$*|' m '&' ns '|' Θ '⍮' Ξ '↘' r" := (eval_apps Θ Ξ m ns r)
with eval_modexp (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : modexp -> env -> dmod -> Prop :=
A module slot is read off the environment.
| eval_me_var :
  `( ⟦ me_var x ⟧ᵐ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ env_mod ρ x )
A unit is a global body module, with no argument yet. Its submodules are selected from it (eval_selm_global).
| eval_me_unit :
  `( ⟦ me_unit fp ⟧ᵐ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ dm_global (q_abs fp nil) nil )
A literal unit is its closure.
| eval_me_lit :
  `( ⟦ Δ ⊢ D ⟧ᶜ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ h ->
     ⟦ me_lit (gu_mk Δ D) ⟧ᵐ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ h )
A submodule is selected from the module's value.
| eval_me_mem :
  `( ⟦ H ⟧ᵐ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ h ->
     h ·ₘ y Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     ⟦ me_mem H y ⟧ᵐ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
An application adds the argument's value to the module's.
| eval_me_app :
  `( ⟦ H ⟧ᵐ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ h ->
     ⟦ N ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ n ->
     $ᵐ| h & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     ⟦ me_app H N ⟧ᵐ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ r )
where "'⟦' H '⟧ᵐ' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' r" := (eval_modexp Θ Ξ H ρ r)
The closure of a unit's definition D lacking the parameters Δ, over ρ: a body, or an alias still lacking a parameter, is its closure; an alias lacking none is its target's value. So no value is a saturated alias.
with eval_close (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : ctx -> moddef -> env -> dmod -> Prop :=
A body: the closure of its expansion, each local open replaced by the definitions it stores (gm_expand)
| eval_close_body :
  `( ⟦ Δ ⊢ md_body sm Φ ⟧ᶜ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ dm_local Δ (md_body sm (gm_expand Φ)) ρ )
An alias still lacking a parameter: its closure
| eval_close_alias :
  `( 0 < List.length Δ ->
     ⟦ Δ ⊢ md_alias E ⟧ᶜ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ dm_local Δ (md_alias E) ρ )
An alias lacking none: its target's value
| eval_close_alias0 :
  `( ⟦ E ⟧ᵐ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ h ->
     ⟦ nil ⊢ md_alias E ⟧ᶜ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ h )
where "'⟦' Δ '⊢' D '⟧ᶜ' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' r" := (eval_close Θ Ξ Δ D ρ r)
Applying a module value to one more argument, which it must still lack.
with eval_appm (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : dmod -> domain -> dmod -> Prop :=
A global module records the argument.
| eval_appm_global :
  `( $ᵐ| dm_global p args & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ dm_global p (args ++ n :: nil) )
A closure takes it as its outermost missing parameter, in its environment.
| eval_appm_local :
  `( ⟦ Δ ⊢ D ⟧ᶜ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↦ n ⦂ entry_type_closure A ρ ↘ r ->
     $ᵐ| dm_local (Δ ++ ce_ass κ A :: nil) D ρ & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
A submodule of an unsaturated module passes it to the module, then selects again.
| eval_appm_member :
  `( $ᵐ| h & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ h' ->
     h' ·ₘ* ch Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     $ᵐ| dm_member h ch & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
where "'$ᵐ|' h '&' n '|' Θ '⍮' Ξ '↘' r" := (eval_appm Θ Ξ h n r)
Applying a module value to arguments, outermost first.
with eval_appms (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : dmod -> list domain -> dmod -> Prop :=
No argument
| eval_appms_nil :
  `( $ᵐ*| h & nil | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ h )
The first argument, then the rest
| eval_appms_cons :
  `( $ᵐ| h & n | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ h1 ->
     $ᵐ*| h1 & ns | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     $ᵐ*| h & n :: ns | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
where "'$ᵐ*|' h '&' ns '|' Θ '⍮' Ξ '↘' r" := (eval_appms Θ Ξ h ns r)
Selecting a term member. A member of a global module is stored closed, over the module's parameters: δ evaluates a transparent one's body in the empty environment, and an opaque one or an axiom is a neutral at its (closed) type. Either is then applied to the module's arguments, once the module lacks none (module_saturated).
with eval_sel (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : dmod -> string -> domain -> Prop :=
A term part of a saturated global module, a transparent definition's body or a definition with a module part's term (gc_term): it, applied to the module's arguments.
| eval_sel_global :
  `( module_saturated Θ Ξ p args ->
     gc_term Θ Ξ (qname_app p (x :: nil)) = Some M ->
     ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ nil ↘ f ->
     $*| f & args | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     dm_global p args ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
An opaque definition or axiom of an evaluated kind of a saturated global module: a neutral, applied to the module's arguments.
| eval_sel_global_neut :
  `( module_saturated Θ Ξ p args ->
     gc_resolve Θ Ξ (qname_app p (x :: nil)) = Some (ge_def b pv κ A B) ->
     evaluated_kind κ ->
     b = false \/ B = None ->
     ⟦ A ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ nil ↘ a ->
     $*| ⇑ a (d_glob (qname_app p (x :: nil))) & args | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     dm_global p args ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
A definition of a global module given exactly its parameters, tagged a proposition, transparent or not: a proof, kept as the selection of the member from the module, over the module's arguments (global_proof_env). Neither its body nor its type is evaluated. Unlike a relevant member, it is not selected from a module given more arguments than it has parameters: a kept proof takes no argument, so there the member of the over-applied module would have a value its spine does not. For example, for module M (a : ℕ) with a theorem h, the ill-typed (M 3) 4 evaluates to dm_global M [3; 4], but a_mem ((M 3) 4) h has no value: its spine reaches the proof at 3 and cannot apply it to 4. So h is not selected from it either.
| eval_sel_global_proof :
  `( gc_loc Θ Ξ p = Some (T, Φ) ->
     List.length args = List.length T ->
     gc_resolve Θ Ξ (qname_app p (x :: nil)) = Some (ge_def b pv ak_propositional A B) ->
     dm_global p args ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ ⋆ᵈ⟨member_proof x, global_proof_env p T args⟩ )
The module of a member of a group of inductive types, as a term, in a saturated global module: the member's type former, applied to the module's arguments.
| eval_sel_global_ind :
  `( module_saturated Θ Ξ p args ->
     gc_resolve Θ Ξ (qname_app p (x :: nil)) = None ->
     ind_mlookup Θ Ξ (qname_app p (x :: nil)) = Some (pq, k, D) ->
     $*| d_ind pq k nil & args | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     dm_global p args ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
A member of a global module lacking a parameter is a member closure.
| eval_sel_global_unsat :
  `( gc_loc Θ Ξ p = Some (T, Φ) ->
     List.length args < List.length T ->
     dm_global p args ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ d_member (dm_global p args) (x :: nil) )
A member of a closure lacking a parameter is a member closure.
| eval_sel_unsat :
  `( 0 < List.length Δ ->
     dm_local Δ D ρ ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ d_member (dm_local Δ D ρ) (x :: nil) )
A term part of a saturated body (entry_tm: a definition's body or a definition with a module part's term): it, in the environment of the body before it, when the entry is relevant. The body is read expanded: evaluated closures are already expanded (eval_close_body), so the expansion here only aligns the relation with kinds (dmod_member_kind_local).
| eval_sel_body :
  `( gm_prefix_upto (gm_expand Φ) x = Some (gm_ext Φ' x E) ->
     entry_tm E = Some (A, M) ->
     evaluated_kind (entry_kind E) ->
     ⟦ Φ' ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ' ->
     ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ' ↘ r ->
     dm_local nil (md_body sm Φ) ρ ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
A definition of a saturated body tagged a proposition: a proof, kept as the selection of the member from the body, its body not evaluated; the environment of the proof is the body's environment extended by the body's closure, so that readback binds the body as its unit over the entries it closes over. The body is read expanded: evaluated closures are already expanded (eval_close_body), so the expansion here only aligns the relation with kinds.
| eval_sel_body_proof :
  `( gm_prefix_upto (gm_expand Φ) x = Some (gm_ext Φ' x E) ->
     entry_tm E = Some (A, M) ->
     entry_kind E = ak_propositional ->
     dm_local nil (md_body sm Φ) ρ ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ ⋆ᵈ⟨member_proof x, ρ ↦ᵐ dm_local nil (md_body sm Φ) ρ ⦂ gu_mk nil (md_body sm Φ)⟩ )
A member of a submodule closure extends the chain.
| eval_sel_member :
  `( dm_member h ch ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ d_member h (ch ++ x :: nil) )
A record type of a saturated global module, stored or with its module's frame open, as a term: its type former, applied to the module's arguments.
| eval_sel_global_record :
  `( module_saturated Θ Ξ p args ->
     gc_resolve Θ Ξ (qname_app p (x :: nil)) = None ->
     record_lookup Θ Ξ (qname_app p (x :: nil)) = Some R ->
     $*| d_record (qname_app p (x :: nil)) nil & args | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     dm_global p args ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
where "h '·ₜ' x Θ '⍮' Ξ '↘' r" := (eval_sel Θ Ξ h x r)
Selecting a submodule.
with eval_selm (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : dmod -> string -> dmod -> Prop :=
A body submodule, an open frame or the module of an inductive type in a global module is a global module, with the same arguments.
| eval_selm_global :
  `( gc_loc Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) = Some TΦ ->
     dm_global p args ·ₘ y Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ dm_global (qname_app p (y :: nil)) args )
An alias submodule of a global module is the closure of the alias, stored closed over the module's parameters, given the module's arguments.
| eval_selm_global_alias :
  `( gc_module Θ Ξ (qname_app p (y :: nil)) = Some (mr_alias (gu_mk Δ D)) ->
     ⟦ Δ ⊢ D ⟧ᶜ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ nil ↘ h ->
     $ᵐ*| h & args | Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     dm_global p args ·ₘ y Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
A submodule of a closure lacking a parameter is a submodule closure.
| eval_selm_unsat :
  `( 0 < List.length Δ ->
     dm_local Δ D ρ ·ₘ y Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ dm_member (dm_local Δ D ρ) (y :: nil) )
A module part of a saturated body (entry_unit: a submodule, or a definition with a module part's): its unit's closure, in the environment of the body before it. The body is read expanded: evaluated closures are already expanded (eval_close_body), so the expansion here only aligns the relation with kinds.
| eval_selm_body :
  `( gm_prefix_upto (gm_expand Φ) y = Some (gm_ext Φ' y E) ->
     entry_unit E = Some (gu_mk Δy Dy) ->
     ⟦ Φ' ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ' ->
     ⟦ Δy ⊢ Dy ⟧ᶜ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ' ↘ r ->
     dm_local nil (md_body sm Φ) ρ ·ₘ y Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
A submodule of a submodule closure extends the chain.
| eval_selm_member :
  `( dm_member h ch ·ₘ y Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ dm_member h (ch ++ y :: nil) )
where "h '·ₘ' y Θ '⍮' Ξ '↘' r" := (eval_selm Θ Ξ h y r)
Selecting along a chain: submodules, then a term member.
with eval_selc (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : dmod -> list string -> domain -> Prop :=
The last selection is a term member.
| eval_selc_one :
  `( h ·ₜ x Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     h ·ₜ* (x :: nil) Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
The ones before it are submodules.
| eval_selc_cons :
  `( h ·ₘ y Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ h1 ->
     h1 ·ₜ* ch Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     h ·ₜ* (y :: ch) Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
where "h '·ₜ*' ch Θ '⍮' Ξ '↘' r" := (eval_selc Θ Ξ h ch r)
with eval_selmc (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : dmod -> list string -> dmod -> Prop :=
The empty chain is the module itself.
| eval_selmc_nil :
  `( h ·ₘ* nil Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ h )
A submodule, then the rest of the chain.
| eval_selmc_cons :
  `( h ·ₘ y Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ h1 ->
     h1 ·ₘ* ch Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r ->
     h ·ₘ* (y :: ch) Θ ⍮ Ξ ↘ r )
where "h '·ₘ*' ch Θ '⍮' Ξ '↘' r" := (eval_selmc Θ Ξ h ch r)
The environment the members of a body see after its entries Φ: each definition adds its value and each module its closure.
with eval_body_env (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) : env -> gmod -> env -> Prop :=
The empty body adds nothing.
| eval_body_env_nil :
  `( ⟦ gm_nil ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ )
A definition tagged an evaluated kind adds its value. A body is read by the kinds its definitions are tagged with, as selection reads it (eval_sel_body): typing makes a definition's tag the kind of its type, a definition an open generates included: the core open phase gives it the type of the member it names (items_gen).
| eval_body_env_def :
  `( evaluated_kind κ ->
     ⟦ Φ ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ1 ->
     ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ1 ↘ m ->
     ⟦ gm_ext Φ y (ge_def b pv κ A (Some M)) ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ1 ↦ m ⦂ entry_type_closure A ρ1 )
A definition tagged a proposition, a proof, adds it kept as it is, unevaluated.
| eval_body_env_def_proof :
  `( ⟦ Φ ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ1 ->
     ⟦ gm_ext Φ y (ge_def b pv ak_propositional A (Some M)) ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ1 ↦ ⋆ᵈ⟨M, ρ1⟩ ⦂ entry_type_closure A ρ1 )
A submodule adds its unit's closure, at the unit.
| eval_body_env_mod :
  `( ⟦ Φ ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ1 ->
     ⟦ Δy ⊢ Dy ⟧ᶜ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ1 ↘ h ->
     ⟦ gm_ext Φ y (ge_mod pm (gu_mk Δy Dy)) ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ1 ↦ᵐ h ⦂ gu_mk Δy Dy )
A definition with a module part adds its term's value and its unit's closure, at the unit.
| eval_body_env_dm :
  `( ⟦ Φ ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ1 ->
     ⟦ M ⟧ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ1 ↘ m ->
     ⟦ Δy ⊢ Dy ⟧ᶜ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ1 ↘ h ->
     ⟦ gm_ext Φ y (ge_def_mod pv A M (gu_mk Δy Dy)) ⟧ᵇ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ρ ↘ ρ1 ↦ᵈ m ⦂ entry_type_closure A ρ1 ‖ h ⦂ gu_mk Δy Dy )
where "'⟦' Φ '⟧ᵇ' Θ '⍮' Ξ '⍮' ρ '↘' ρ'" := (eval_body_env Θ Ξ ρ Φ ρ').
